brief.scope: Test-system census of every file under ops/**/tests/ and .claude/skills/*/tests/, per the work order in in/. The categories, disjoint: (1) world-building: HOME, XDG roots, temp root, cwd or environment set by hand in the test versus through a shared helper; (2) counterparty simulation: fake programs embedded as string constants or planted executables, each with its own call log, failure injection or cleanup; (3) subprocess and resource ownership: run or Popen without a reap, close or timeout policy; (4) representation pins: assertions on a whole serialization, a count, a path, a timestamp or a digest where the contract does not own that value; (5) regression-per-file: a test file that exists for one ledger row (LD-n) or one PR and rebuilds a world or a fake to do it; (6) support already generic: helpers used by two or more families that belong in a shared kit. Write out/census.json in the shape the work order gives; every finding names its files and carries a reproduce command.

findings.claim: Category (3), subprocess/resource ownership: 171 subprocess.run calls across 58 files have no timeout keyword, so a wedged git, gh, cue, jq, shell, or subject process can hang the suite indefinitely.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'import ast,pathlib,subprocess; ps=subprocess.check_output(["git","ls-files","ops/**/tests/*.py",".claude/skills/*/tests/*.py"],text=True).splitlines(); rows=[(p,[n.lineno for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(pathlib.Path(p).read_text())) if isinstance(n,ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func,ast.Attribute) and isinstance(n.func.value,ast.Name) and n.func.value.id=="subprocess" and n.func.attr=="run" and all(k.arg!="timeout" for k in n.keywords)]) for p in ps]; print("\n".join(f"{p}:{chr(44).join(map(str,ls))}" for p,ls in rows if ls))'

findings.claim: Category (3), subprocess/resource ownership: the stall-test timeout branch kills the breaker child and immediately raises self.fail without wait or communicate, leaving that child unreaped precisely on the failure path.

Category (4), representation pins: 31 assertions pin corpus/table cardinalities that the governing behavior contracts do not own; adding a valid row changes the representation and forces unrelated count updates.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'import ast,pathlib,re,subprocess; ps=subprocess.check_output(["git","ls-files","ops/**/tests/*.py",".claude/skills/*/tests/*.py"],text=True).splitlines(); ns=("len(corpus.","corpus.COUNTS[","len(CASES),10","must_flag,4","must_not,6","len(PROBE_IDS),9","len(NAME_KEYS),5","len(self.CASES),4"); print("\n".join(f"{p}:{n.lineno}" for p in ps for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(pathlib.Path(p).read_text())) if isinstance(n,ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func,ast.Attribute) and n.func.attr=="assertEqual" and any(x in re.sub(r"\s+","",ast.unparse(n)) for x in ns)))'

findings.claim: Category (5), regression-per-file: 14 modules whose module docstring names one LD row or PR also rebuild a temporary world or embed a fake program, preserving issue/PR-specific fixture islands instead of adding the regression to an existing family fixture.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'import ast,pathlib,re,subprocess; ps=subprocess.check_output(["git","ls-files","ops/**/tests/*.py",".claude/skills/*/tests/*.py"],text=True).splitlines(); print("\n".join(p for p in ps if re.search(r"LD-\d+|PR\s*#?\s*\d+",ast.get_docstring(ast.parse(pathlib.Path(p).read_text()),clean=False) or "",re.I) and re.search(r"TemporaryDirectory\(|mkdtemp\(|#!",pathlib.Path(p).read_text())))'
